mappings.applicability_reason: This threat concerns interception or compromise of invoice details as they are sent from the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) to a hosted model provider (cmp-003) over df-002, and does not involve any administrative or operator interface, so the requirement’s conditions about privileged administrative access are not engaged for this threat.

Although users submit invoice JSON that is passed through the agent workflow to the model [evd-002, evd-004, evd-005], this threat is specifically about an on-path attacker or compromised model environment reading or tampering with invoice details in transit, not about instructions embedded in content altering the model’s task, so the prompt-injection-focused requirement is not engaged by this threat.

The threat addresses confidentiality and integrity of invoice details between the agent and the hosted model provider, not automatic publication of model output to an external destination without human review; the workflow describes the agent responding with a decision in the same conversation [evd-002], so this publication-focused requirement does not bear on this threat.

Invoice content supplied by users is parsed and the resulting invoice details (amount, submitter, category, due date) are sent from the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) to an external hosted model provider (cmp-003) for analysis [evd-001, evd-004, evd-005], so customer content crosses a model-provider boundary and the requirement to document what is sent and why that scope is necessary applies; the documentation describes that only parsed invoice details are returned to the model but does not explain why that scope is necessary, so the requirement is only partially satisfied.

The described threat stops at the point where invoice details are transmitted from the agent to the hosted model provider and processed there; it does not involve rendering model output into a user interface or external markup, so the output-encoding requirement does not bear on this threat.

The threat concerns protection of invoice details on data flow df-002 between the Invoice Agent and the hosted model provider, independent of how end users authenticate; whether user authentication is delegated or local does not meaningfully affect interception or tampering on this outbound service call, so this requirement does not apply to this threat.

This threat does not involve any privileged or administrative interface; it describes normal invoice processing and the subsequent call from the Invoice Agent to the hosted model provider, so multi-factor authentication for administrative or externally reachable privileged access is outside the scope of this threat.

The threat is about confidentiality and integrity of invoice details in transit to an external model provider and does not involve cross-tenant data access or authorization decisions between tenants, so tenant-aware authorization is not engaged for this specific threat path.

While the agent holds credentials for the hosted model provider [evd-006], the described threat focuses on interception or compromise of invoice details in transit, not on over-broad delegated privileges to an external platform, so limiting integration scopes does not directly bear on this threat.

The attack path for this threat does not involve the build or deployment pipeline; it assumes a running Invoice Agent that sends invoice details to a hosted model provider, so controls on pipeline authentication and dependency management do not affect whether invoice details can be intercepted or altered in transit.

Invoice JSON documents with business invoice details [evd-002, evd-004, evd-005] are sent from the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) to an external hosted model provider (cmp-003) over internet-exposed data flow df-002, so confidential customer data crosses a network boundary the system does not control, matching this requirement’s applicable_conditions; the documentation does not state whether this traffic is encrypted in transit or how any at-rest protection is provided, so satisfaction is unverified for this threat.

The threat description is limited to exposure or tampering of invoice details while they are in transit between the Invoice Agent and the hosted model provider; while traces of HTTP bodies are captured for debugging [evd-006], the risk being modelled here is not about retention duration or deletion of stored working copies, so this retention-focused requirement does not bear on this specific threat.

This threat is about interception or compromise of invoice details on an outbound call to an external model provider, not about separation of stored artifacts belonging to different tenants in a shared storage system, so the tenant-separation requirement does not apply to this threat path.

The threat scenario does not involve customer-initiated or operator-initiated deletion of stored invoice data; it focuses on exposure and tampering during transmission to the hosted model provider, so the requirement on documenting deletion paths for stored customer data is not engaged by this threat.

Although request and tool-call traces, including HTTP bodies, are captured for debugging [evd-006], this specific threat models an attacker intercepting or tampering with invoice details in transit to the hosted model provider, not compromise of the observability platform or leakage via logs, so the logging-content requirement is not engaged for this threat.

No administrative or operator interface is involved in the described attack path, which concerns automated invoice processing and the call to the hosted model provider, so requirements about auditing security-relevant administrative actions do not apply to this threat.

The threat concerns an internet-exposed outbound data flow from the Invoice Agent to an external hosted model provider, not the network placement of internal data stores, queues, caches, or internal services, so the internal-network-segmentation requirement does not bear on this threat.

The agent runs with credentials for the model provider and observability service [evd-006], but the threat under evaluation assumes those credentials are already in use and focuses on interception or tampering of invoice details in transit, not compromise of where long-lived credentials are stored, so this secret-storage requirement is not engaged for this threat.

Whether the model provider credentials are short-lived or long-lived affects the impact of credential compromise but does not change the attack where an on-path attacker or compromised provider reads or alters invoice details on df-002, so this requirement about credential lifetime does not bear directly on the threat described.

Invoice details derived from customer-submitted invoices are sent from the Invoice Agent to an external hosted model provider for processing [evd-001, evd-005], so customer data crosses an external-processor boundary and the requirement to document what is sent and the provider’s retention and usage terms applies; the documentation does not describe whether or how the provider retains or uses this data beyond serving the request, so satisfaction is unverified for this threat.

The threat focuses on confidentiality and integrity of invoice details when calling the hosted model provider, not on unbounded consumption of a metered external service or retries triggered by external events, so the requirement to bound work triggered by external events does not apply to this threat.

The architecture and threat describe the Invoice Agent initiating requests to a hosted model provider [evd-001, evd-005, evd-006]; there is no inbound event endpoint accepting callbacks from an external platform in this threat path, so the webhook-origin-verification requirement does not bear on this threat.

Because the threat involves outbound requests from the Invoice Agent to a hosted model provider rather than inbound state-changing events delivered to the system, requirements about preventing or absorbing replay of inbound events are not engaged for this threat.

documentation_gaps.title: Encryption and authentication of df-002 (Invoice Agent to hosted model provider) are undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: Invoice details derived from customer-submitted invoices are sent from the Invoice Agent (cmp-001) to an external hosted model provider (cmp-003) for processing over internet-exposed data flow df-002 [evd-001, evd-005, evd-006], and the flow’s encryption_in_transit and authentication properties are recorded as unknown in the approved context. Documentation does not state whether transport encryption (for example, TLS) and request authentication are enforced on this flow, so the assessment cannot determine whether requirement req-DATA-001 is satisfied for threat thr-002.
documentation_gaps.importance: Needed to evaluate whether confidentiality and integrity of invoice data on df-002 are adequately protected, and to know if additional controls are required to mitigate interception or tampering in transit.
requested_evidence: Data flow or deployment documentation specifying the protocol, transport encryption (such as TLS configuration), and authentication mechanism used for df-002 between cmp-001 and cmp-003, including any model-provider endpoint configuration.

documentation_gaps.title: Hosted model provider retention and usage of invoice data are undocumented
documentation_gaps.description: The documentation states that the Invoice Agent sends parsed invoice details to a hosted model provider for processing [evd-001, evd-005] but does not describe whether the provider retains this customer data, for how long, or whether it is used for any purpose beyond serving the request. Without this information, the assessment cannot determine whether requirement req-TPI-001 is satisfied for threat thr-002.
documentation_gaps.importance: Provider retention and secondary use of invoice data affect the long-term confidentiality impact if the hosted model provider or its environment is compromised, which is part of the concern captured in this threat.
requested_evidence: A summary of the hosted model provider’s data handling terms for this integration, including what invoice data is sent, whether it is retained, retention duration, and whether it is used for training or other purposes beyond serving the request.
